thesis: Purest large-cap leverage to a structural copper deficit; the Grasberg guidance cut is now in the price ahead of the July 23 Q2 print, with the street ($67.90 consensus, $75–77 at UBS/Barclays) above spot.
markdown:
## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
**BUY** with $70 price target (+13.8% from $61.52, as of 7/10/26) over 12 months. Freeport is the cleanest large-cap expression of the copper electrification/AI-infrastructure demand story. The stock is down ~8.8% over the past month after management cut 2026 Grasberg volumes, but the reset guidance de-risks the July 23 Q2 print, US operations are performing, and Grasberg still ramps toward near-full production by late 2027. Risk-reward is favorable with the street consensus ($67.90–$68.27) above spot and recent initiations higher (Barclays Overweight $77; UBS Buy $75).

## FUNDAMENTAL ANALYSIS
**Recent Financial Metrics**: Q2 2026 consensus calls for EPS of $0.58 (+7.4% YoY) on revenue of ~$6.4B (−15.6% YoY), the revenue decline reflecting the Grasberg volume reset. Q1 2026 delivered strong earnings but was overshadowed by the Grasberg delay disclosure (per company slides/8-K). Market cap ~$82B.

**Production & Guidance**: 2026 copper sales guidance cut to ~3.1B lbs and gold to ~650k oz. PT Freeport Indonesia (PTFI) is now expected at ~0.7B lbs copper and ~650k oz gold for 2026, down from January estimates of 0.9B lbs and 0.8M oz, on wet-ore conditions and ore-loading infrastructure modifications at the Grasberg Block Cave. Management continues to guide the district toward near-full production by late 2027.

**Peer Comparison**: Among the majors (BHP ~$180B, RIO ~$140B, Glencore ~$92B), FCX carries the highest revenue sensitivity to copper price per share — the reason to own it in a copper-led cycle, and the reason it de-rates hardest when the metal corrects.

**Forward Outlook**: Copper ~$6.00/lb in early July (two-week low) after record highs earlier in 2026; Goldman Sachs sees prices declining somewhat from records but staying historically elevated. Chinese buyers (~60% of global demand) have been buying the dip. Cost watch-item: Strait of Hormuz disruption has spiked sulfuric acid prices (~$820/t Middle East, ~$1,200/t Brazil), a refining input.

## CATALYST ANALYSIS
**Near-term (0–6 months)**: Q2 2026 earnings July 23 — guidance reset lowers the bar; any confirmation that Block Cave ore-loading fixes are on schedule is a positive surprise. Copper price response to China stimulus headlines.
**Medium-term (6–24 months)**: Grasberg ramp toward near-full production by late 2027; US brownfield/leaching volume additions; potential US copper policy support (tariffs/critical-minerals incentives).
**Event-driven**: Indonesia fiscal/contract developments around PTFI; M&A in the copper space repricing scarce large-scale assets.

## VALUATION & PRICE TARGETS
Street consensus ~$67.90–$68.27 (MarketBeat/MarketScreener aggregates); Barclays initiated Overweight at $77; UBS raised to $75 (Buy). LIQD base case $70 assumes copper holds $5.50–6.25/lb and Grasberg ramp milestones are met. Bull case $77 on copper back above $6.50/lb with a clean ramp. Bear case $52 on copper below $5/lb or a further Grasberg setback. Probability weighting: 25%/50%/25%.

## RISK ASSESSMENT
**Company risks**: Grasberg execution (wet-ore/infrastructure fixes; a second guidance cut would be severely punished), Indonesian regulatory and fiscal terms, concentration of value in a single district.
**Macro risks**: Copper price (the dominant driver), China demand, USD strength, global manufacturing cycle; input-cost inflation via sulfuric acid and energy.
**Position sizing**: 2–4% given high beta to copper; stage entries around the July 23 print.

## TECHNICAL CONTEXT & OPTIONS INTELLIGENCE
Stock +1.64% on 7/10/26 to $61.52 but −8.8% over the trailing month; the post-guidance-cut gap (−11% on the cut) is the key overhead supply zone. Options flow and short-interest data not sourced in this run — n/a.

## MARKET POSITIONING
Copper equities have outperformed bulk-commodity miners YTD as the market pays for electrification leverage and avoids China property exposure. FCX is the default large-cap copper allocation for US institutions; positioning washouts around guidance cuts (like the current one) have historically been the entry.
